title: 🔋 The Honor 700 is coming with a 9,000 mAh battery — official reveal November 23!
body: 🔋 The Honor 700 is coming with a 9,000 mAh battery — official reveal November 23!
Honor announced it will unveil three new phones — the Honor 700, 700 Pro and 700S — in China on November 23, at an event in Wuhan starting at 2:30 p.m. local time.

The company confirmed that all three phones carry a 9,000 mAh "Qinghai Lake" battery, a huge capacity that puts the series at the front of big-battery phones, and confirmed that the whole series runs on Snapdragon processors.

According to reports, the three phones share a 6.57-inch display, a 50-megapixel front camera and a body 7.96 mm thick, running MagicOS 11 based on Android 17, with 80W wired charging and weights between 208 and 213 grams.

The differences between the models appear in the processor and camera: the Pro version carries the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor with memory up to 16 GB and storage up to 512 GB, the standard version has the Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 processor, and the 700S version has the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 processor. All three models share — according to reports — a 200-megapixel main camera, with a 50-megapixel periscope camera and 3.5x optical zoom on the 700 and 700 Pro models.

The company also teased an AI-powered small display built into the rear camera unit, without yet explaining exactly what this display does. Honor has not yet announced any plans to launch the series outside China.

Simply put: imagine a phone that runs two or three days without a charger, because its battery is almost twice that of most phones. That is Honor's bet: that you forget the charger for days, not hours.
Is a 9,000 mAh battery enough for you to choose this phone, or are the camera and processor more important to you than the battery?
